summary: Lccimio, the Long Shore: a council of elder houses, orchards and white quays, a watch on the rift and a patient road to the Kindred.

lusmios_counsel_spirit.name: Lusmio's Counsel
lusmios_counsel_spirit.desc: The oldest voice in the Elders' hall teaches the younger houses to wait, and what they wait for tends to arrive.

old_houses.name: The Old Houses Hold
old_houses.desc: The council keeps its ancient order, and the shore is stubborn in defence of its customs.

open_houses.name: The Open Houses
open_houses.desc: Young houses and newcomers sit in council, and ideas travel from the quays to the high seats.

wellsprings.name: Wellsprings of the Shore
wellsprings.desc: Walled and kept springs lift the craft of every workshop that draws from them.

long_shore_prospers.name: The Long Shore Prospers
long_shore_prospers.desc: Rich quays and busy yards: building goes quickly, though the shore buys more luxuries than it used to.

rift_watch.name: The Watch on the Rift
rift_watch.desc: Lantern-keepers on every headland see ships long before the ships see the shore.

elder_wardens_spirit.name: Elder Wardens
elder_wardens_spirit.desc: Old wardens teach the young the long patience of a defence that never stops.

shore_holds.name: The Shore Holds
shore_holds.desc: The wardens have thrown the landing back into the sea, and every grove stands as a wall behind them.

elders_gather.title: The Elders Gather
elders_gather.desc: The Elders of Lccimio gather beneath the old lantern-trees, and the first matter is the order of speaking. Lusmio waits until the murmuring settles before he asks who will begin.

eastern_quays.title: Talk on the Eastern Quays
eastern_quays.desc: Merchants home from the far quays tell a tale that sits ill with the harbour-masters. Courts across the rift are buying timber, rope and steersmen, and nobody can say whom the ships are for.

pilgrims_pass.title: Pilgrims on the Shore Road
pilgrims_pass.desc: A long line of pilgrims in grey walks the Shore Road toward the Zilin Hills, bound for the hermitage of [zin_loc_deliverer]. They are polite and footsore, they buy bread at every orchard gate, and they ask for nothing else.

focuses.name: The Elders of Lccimio
focuses.desc: The elder houses of the Long Shore sit beneath the lantern-trees, and Elder Lusmio calls them to order. On this shore nobody decides alone what the houses may decide together.

focuses.name: Lusmio's Counsel
focuses.desc: Lusmio has sat in council longer than Aenor has had its present dynasty, and he remembers what each house promised and in which year. His patience is the shore's slowest and surest tool.

focuses.name: Houses of the Long Shore
focuses.desc: Orchard-houses, quay-houses and wellspring-houses each keep a seat and a grudge. A fixed place at the table for every house quiets the quarrels before they begin.

focuses.name: The Patient Council
focuses.desc: The Elders never hurry. A matter that takes seven meetings is settled for seven generations, and the shore has learned to prefer it that way.

focuses.name: The Old Houses Hold
focuses.desc: The oldest houses keep the council's old order: speech by age, decision by agreement, and nothing altered that the dead would not recognise.

focuses.name: The Open Houses
focuses.desc: Young houses and newcomers from the quays are given seats and a voice. The council loses a little of its solemnity and gains a great deal of news.

focuses.name: Council of the Long Shore
focuses.desc: With the houses agreed on how they sit, the council speaks for the whole shore, from the first orchard to the last white quay.

focuses.name: Groves of Lccimio
focuses.desc: The orchard groves that give the shore its wealth are tended again in their old rows, and a pressing-house is raised where the best fruit is brought.

focuses.name: Wellsprings of the Shore
focuses.desc: Clear springs rise along the shore road. Each is walled, named and kept by one family, and every workshop that draws their water works the better for it.

focuses.name: Orchard Roads
focuses.desc: Paved lanes run between the orchard rows so that carts may reach the quays in any weather. The first frost no longer spoils a season's fruit.

focuses.name: Shipwrights of the Shore
focuses.desc: The only elven sails on the rift are built in Lccimio's yards, on keels of timber the groves give willingly, and every hull is blessed before it meets the water.

focuses.name: Grove Workshops
focuses.desc: Joiners, coopers and weavers set up under the orchard eaves, working the wood and fibre the groves shed. Nothing is felled that has not first fallen.

focuses.name: The Long Shore Prospers
focuses.desc: Fruit, cloth and timber go out from the white quays, and silver comes home. The shore is rich, and for once it says so aloud.

focuses.name: The Watch on the Rift
focuses.desc: The rift sea is narrow here, and the elders remember how quickly a narrow sea can be crossed. Lantern-keepers are set on every headland to watch the far water.

focuses.name: Beacons of Lccimio
focuses.desc: Stone beacons rise on the headlands, each in sight of the next, ready to carry a warning from the last quay to the council hall before the tide turns.

focuses.name: Elven Sails of the Shore
focuses.desc: The shipwrights lay down hulls meant to go out and look, not to stay and fight. White sails are sewn for the long crossing that nobody on the shore has yet needed to make.

focuses.name: Talk on the Eastern Quays
focuses.desc: Merchants home from the far quays speak of courts across the rift gathering timber, rope and steersmen. Nobody can say who the ships are for, and nobody likes not knowing.

focuses.name: Shore Wardens
focuses.desc: Wardens are posted along the whole length of the shore road, with bows, signal horns and orders to light the beacons at the first strange keel.

focuses.name: Kin of the Woods
focuses.desc: Lccimio sends its elders to the great groves of the Magical Forest with fruit, wine and an open hand. The kin of the woods are slow to forget, and slower to refuse.

focuses.name: Answer the Elder Moot
focuses.desc: When the Elder Moot calls the realms to speak with one voice, Lccimio does not leave the answer to others. Its elders ride to the moot with their houses behind them.

focuses.name: Songs with the Forest
focuses.desc: Choirs of the Long Shore learn the warding-songs of the great forest, and the old protections are sung over the headlands at the turn of every season.

focuses.name: Wardens for the Passes
focuses.desc: Far to the south, in the high valleys of Nolorim, the towers on the passes have too few wardens. Lccimio sends a company from the shore, and the kin remember it.

focuses.name: Stand with the Kindred
focuses.desc: The Kindred of the Woods has been raised, to defend elven land and nothing beyond it. Lccimio takes its place among the kin, and no man is asked to stand beside them.

focuses.name: Healers of Lccimio
focuses.desc: The shore has more healers than wars to heal. Lccimio sends the surplus abroad, one by one, to wherever the sick are many and the herbs are few.

focuses.name: The Wizard's Trail
focuses.desc: Old rolls speak of a wanderer who once knew the cure for every curse. Lccimio's scholars follow the rumour road by road, and learn a good deal on the way, though not where it ends.

focuses.name: The Refusal Kept
focuses.desc: The question is put again whether the elves owe men anything. The Elders answer as their grandfathers did: healers may go, hosts may not, and the shore will say so plainly.

focuses.name: Wardens for Friends
focuses.desc: Single wardens, bound to no banner, go out to the friends who ask for them. They carry bows and herbs, and they go as guests, not as an army.

focuses.name: Pilgrims on the Shore Road
focuses.desc: Grey-robed pilgrims have begun to walk the Shore Road toward the Zilin Hills. The orchard gates stay open to them, and the Elders have not yet decided what that means.

focuses.name: Keep the Roads Open
focuses.desc: The roads stay free to any footsore traveller. A shore that turns away the weary has forgotten what its wellsprings are for.

focuses.name: Toll the Pilgrims
focuses.desc: A toll-house is built at the road's first bridge. Pilgrims may pass, but each pays a small coin, and the Elders put it to the upkeep of the road.

focuses.name: The Temple on the Road
focuses.desc: Word comes out of the Zilin Hills that the hermitage of [zin_loc_deliverer] is no house of peace. The Elders close the Shore Road to pilgrims and turn the footsore back with water, not welcome.

focuses.name: Wardens of Lccimio
focuses.desc: The wardens of the Long Shore are few, quiet and very good. They are drilled in the orchards, in the rain, and taught to shoot at what they cannot yet see.

focuses.name: Longbow Companies
focuses.desc: Bowyers of the shore cut yew from the oldest rows and string their bows with silk from the quay-looms. Each company draws its own mark.

focuses.name: Grove Riders
focuses.desc: White deer are gentled in the high orchards, trained to carry a rider through the trees without sound. They are a scout's mount, never a charger's.

focuses.name: Elder Wardens
focuses.desc: The oldest wardens teach the youngest in the rhythms of a long defence. They have not fought in generations, and they have forgotten none of it.

focuses.name: The Rift Burns
focuses.desc: Black sails fill the narrow water. The beacons are lit from the first headland to the last, and the whole shore wakes to the sound of horns.

focuses.name: Every Grove a Fortress
focuses.desc: Every orchard is made a stronghold, with its lanes barred, its wells covered and its tallest trees manned with archers.

focuses.name: The Kin Ride to the Shore
focuses.desc: Word has reached the great groves, and the kin come down to the coast with their bows. Where the Refusal forbids armies abroad, it has never forbidden armies at home.

focuses.name: Into the Rift Sea
focuses.desc: The wardens throw the first landing back into the water, and the shore holds. The Elders ask only that it hold for a year more.

focuses.name: The Shore Is Quiet
focuses.desc: The last ship has left the horizon, and no banner of the east remains in the war. The beacons are put out one by one, and the orchards bloom without a guard.
